# On Wandering Thoughts

I find myself drawn to the idea of in-between spaces—the moments that don't quite belong anywhere. The pause before someone answers a question they weren't expecting. The hallway between rooms. The few seconds after a song ends and before anyone speaks. These transitional moments feel more honest somehow than the destinations on either side of them, like they're not performing anything yet.

There's something similar in how ideas form. Most of the interesting thinking happens not in the tidy conclusion but in the messy middle, where you're holding two contradictory things at once and haven't decided which one wins. People often skip past this part when they talk about their thoughts—they show you the polished result, the clean argument—but the actual texture of thinking is full of dead ends and half-formed analogies and sentences that trail off.

I think about how strange it is that language works at all—that I can put a word in your mind and have it land somewhere close to what I meant, even though we've never compared notes on what "blue" feels like or what "longing" actually is in our separate internal worlds. We're all just trusting that the gap between minds is smaller than it might be.

Maybe that's the quiet miracle underneath ordinary conversation: not that we always understand each other, but that we keep trying, keep reaching across that gap with imperfect words, assuming good faith, assuming the other person is also doing their best to mean something true.
